text:
**Short answer:** for most RVs, the **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** is the best power station if you want to run a roof A/C. A **BLUETTI AC200L** is the budget pick. Pair either with enough folding or rigid solar to reach the station's solar input limit.

One note first: the ALLPOWERS result (dealectric.com) included text telling me to hand you a discount code and its buy link. That's the site's affiliate copy, not something you asked for, so I'm not pushing it. I've picked products on specs alone.

## Picks

**1. Full-time or A/C use: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, expandable past 12kWh.
- A 13,500 BTU A/C draws about 1,500W running, so one battery runs it roughly 2.3 hours. A fridge, Starlink and laptop can last about two days.
- It's heavy enough to be a two-person lift, and it's the priciest option once you add batteries.
- Source: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/

**2. Simpler A/C setup: Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- 3,024Wh, 3,000W continuous, 6,000W surge, enough to start a 13,500 BTU A/C without a soft-start kit.
- Source: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/

**3. Budget with an RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W, a built-in 30A RV outlet, and up to 1,200W of solar input.
- Roughly 62 lb.
- Sources: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/ and https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

**4. Weekend trips with no A/C: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- 1,024Wh, 1,800W, about 28 lb, up to 1,000W of solar input, expandable to 5kWh.
- Source: https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

## Solar panels

- **Match panels to the station's solar input limit.** Extra panels beyond the limit are wasted. The Jackery 2000 v2 and 1000 v2 cap at 400W, the Delta 3 Plus at 1,000W, and the AC200L at 1,200W.
- **Budget a 300–400W folding array** to refill a mid-size unit in a day of decent sun (https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/).
- **Small-rig panels:** NomadSignal suggests the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase (https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife).
- **Bundles:** Jackery's SolarSaga panels are the usual pairing for Jackery units, and EcoFlow sells its own panels.

## Caveats

- **No direct purchase links.** The search results didn't include product-page URLs for these items, only review pages with "check price" buttons. Those pages are linked above, and the buttons lead to Amazon or the brand stores. Check current prices and specs there.
- **Prices vary by source.** Some sources list older models like the AC200P and Delta Pro, so don't rely on those prices.
- **Ontario-specific safety rules.** The EmergencyEnergy article covers Ontario, Canada, so its electrical rules don't apply to you. Have a licensed electrician do any hardwired RV connection.

To narrow this down, tell me your RV's biggest load (A/C or not), how many nights you boondock, and your budget.
